openings.claim: A decision-bound frontier may make scarce adjudications more informative than prioritizing the slice with the largest apparent gain.
openings.delta: Change the carrier from provisional confusion counts to per-record uncertainty intervals. Equal baseline/candidate predictions contribute zero regardless of label; unresolved flagged records with different predictions contribute conservatively between minus one and plus one. Aggregate total and slice bounds. Select a flagged row whose possible resolutions most change certification of an acceptance clause, breaking ties by record identifier.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, a fixed ordering of flagged rows from the largest apparent-gain slice first, frontier selection may certify more supported decisions within sixteen adjudications. The differing observation is a frozen supported verdict versus unresolved, checked against the full-label key. This advantage is hypothetical.
openings.probe: Run both selection policies on the matched copies after the same four rows are withheld. Maintain a ledger of identifier, selection reason, access outcome, adjudication count and elapsed time. Advance only when the total lower bound is at least four and every slice lower bound is at least minus two. Reject only when the total upper bound is below four or some slice upper bound is below minus two. Otherwise continue until sixteen adjudications or seventy minutes, then report unresolved and affected slices. Freeze both reports before opening the full-label key; compare supported-verdict correctness, unresolved outcomes, adjudications and time.
assumptions: Unflagged supplied labels are fixed review inputs; uncertainty concerns the flagged labels.
Conservative bounds can remain inconclusive even when a joint analysis could decide.

The opening loses its advantage if influential rows are withheld, the rival selects equivalent rows, or bounds remain inconclusive after the allowed work. Neither certification nor deployment readiness is promised.

assessment: One probe-ready workflow hypothesis; all resources are synthetic stipulations. Interval certificates preserve the acceptance thresholds and abstain when remaining uncertainty prevents support.
